title: King Oliver, and Louis Armstrong as singer and showman
summary: He heard Oliver's cliches in Armstrong's playing, and describes Louis's singing and joking nature as extraordinary.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yes, now how did you like King Oliver?

I liked King Oliver, but he never played too much when I would go to listen to him. Cause it was mostly an ensemble band, but he played like short solos. I thought he was a very, very fine. And I could hear Joe Oliver's playing, (unintelligible) in Louis Armstrong's playing until he died. I could hear little things. They were little cliches that they would have among themselves. Red Allen has it too.
Little things that probably nobody else would pay attention to.
Well, I thought it was sensational. It was sensational, right from the beginning. I don't think anybody found anything wrong with it.
Well, he was such a showman, very outgoing.
Oh, yes, he was a showman, in fact anything Louis Armstrong did was a sensation.

Anything he did. Even on the streets, he would walk up the street, laughing and joking, his belly shaking fat, you know, and he was just a funny, jolly fellow all the way around. Everything he said was funny.

Joking, wonderful jokes, you know. He was just an ordinary -- extraordinary man. And I don't think anybody ever will be able to play like him. I didn't have any idea of ever playing like him, but I wanted to get in there and see what was inside of it, you know. Not only Louis, but you could hear lot of this same things among, with Joe Oliver, Red Allen, Bob Scheffner, they all had something in common.
